headline: NEW -- IRGC claims 3 tankers hit mines south of Hormuz in past 24h
dek: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM + ATTRIBUTED REPORT] Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Thursday that three oil tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting sea mines while attempting to cross an unauthorised route south of the Strait of Hormuz over the past 24 hours (Arab News Oct 29, updated 11:57 AST =…
fault_line: Are the tankers hitting US-cleared lanes' mines, or is Tehran inventing mine strikes to scare shipping off its unauthorised route?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM + ATTRIBUTED REPORT] Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Thursday that three oil tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting sea mines while attempting to cross an unauthorised route south of the Strait of Hormuz over the past 24 hours (Arab News Oct 29, updated 11:57 AST = 12:57 , carrying the IRGC statement via Iranian state media; Devdiscourse syndicated carry 14:21 IST = 12:51 , same story, NOT an independent family). Per the IRGC, the tankers had switched off radar/navigation systems and ignored Guards navy warnings, and were abandoned on the southern shores of the strait. No vessel names, flags, casualties or casualty figures are given in the retrieved reports. Separately, UKMTO said Thursday a ship on fire was reported in the Strait, spotted 9 nautical miles north of Oman's Khasab, reported by another ship's master, WITHOUT giving cause or casualties -- UKMTO corroborates a fire report only, NOT the mine cause. COUNTERPOINT: CENTCOM's standing Oct 28 denial (recorded totw-20261029-0100-02, HOLD) says all primary Hormuz routes were cleared of mines by US forces and remain clear and calls Iranian mine claims FALSE; Axar.az Oct 29 re-carries that CENTCOM position (undeclared tier, not counted, and not confirmed as a fresh Oct 29 statement -- do NOT present the denial as new). PORTWATCH BACKBONE: newest snapshot portwatch-2026-10-26.json is STALE (latest observation 2026-10-18): it counted 4 Hormuz transits on Oct 18, 7-day average 3.71 vs 2025 baseline 85.53/day -- STALE, never cited as live. A separate undeclared tracker (hormuz.now) reports 5 crossings on Oct 29 to 07:44 UTC (2 in, 3 out, 3 tankers) and a 7-day average of 6.4/day (~8% of its pre-crisis 84.8); that tracker is NOT PortWatch and NOT a registry tier, so it is context only and never a counted PortWatch figure. This is a NEW claim distinct from the Oct 27 single-tanker mine-fire claim and the Oct 17 two-supertanker claim already recorded.
sections.what_verified: IRGC statement via Arab News (T3) + Devdiscourse syndication of the same story (1 family for the mine cause); UKMTO (T1) corroborates a Thursday fire report only, not mines. CENTCOM denial is the standing Oct 28 position, re-carried Oct 29 by undeclared Axar.az.
sections.what_disputed: CENTCOM Oct 28: routes cleared, Iranian mine claims FALSE, 'thousands' transited safely (claimant figure, not a counted figure). IRGC gives no vessel names, flags or casualties; UKMTO gives no cause. Mine cause is therefore unverified, and CENTCOM's 'thousands' is equally uncounted against stale PortWatch data.
sections.why_matters: Hormuz claim vs denial, counted against stale PortWatch: 3 tankers 'mined' vs CENTCOM 'routes clear' -- the fire off Khasab is real, the mine cause is not proven.
sections.context: Background: NEW -- IRGC claims 3 tankers hit mines south of Hormuz in past 24h; UKMTO reports ship on fire off Khasab; CENTCOM denial stands

totw_analysis: Our read: Hormuz claim vs denial, counted against stale PortWatch: 3 tankers 'mined' vs CENTCOM 'routes clear' -- the fire off Khasab is real, the mine cause is not proven. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Are the tankers hitting US-cleared lanes' mines, or is Tehran inventing mine strikes to scare shipping off its unauthorised route?
